# Kling 4 prompting guide — key frames first, short director's prompts

**Two to four key stills plus a short director's prompt become cinematic Kling 4 takes instead of flat, slow-motion AI video.**

<p><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/194b94d0-58ff-4e8b-91de-4f1959d04013/file_d76861a123c6.webp" alt="Kling 4 shot from key frames: a skateboarder ollies past a yellow Lisbon tram in a wide fisheye shot, low to the cobbles." width="480"></p>

How to prompt Kling 4 (Kling 4.0, kling_v4) for cinematic AI video that does not look like AI slop: let a strong image model compose every shot, then give Kling 4 two to four key frames and a short director's prompt. Covers reference-to-video inputs (@Image, @Element, @Video, @Voice), multi-shot prompts with seconds, 30-second takes, dialogue in quotes, "no slow motion", lens and film-look lines, prompts that fail and their rewrites, elements that need two photos, the failure fixes (slow motion by default, six fingers, AI-smooth framing, face drift in close-ups) and the exact varg call with the reference route pinned. Use when someone asks how to prompt Kling 4, why Kling 4 looks worse than Seedance 2.5, how to use Kling 4 reference-to-video, elements, multi_prompt or keyframes, or wants a Kling 4 prompt written. For a whole short film use kling-4-keyframe-film; for a 30-second action montage use kling-4-action-montage.

```bash
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill kling-4-prompting                # Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini CLI, OpenCode…
gh skill install vargHQ/skills kling-4-prompting --agent github-copilot --scope user
# or all 83 skills as a Claude Code plugin:
claude plugin marketplace add vargHQ/skills
claude plugin install varg@varg
```

## Ask your agent

- "Write a Kling 4 prompt for the three stills in ./frames/: she walks into the diner and orders coffee, 15 seconds, 21:9"
- "My Kling 4 clips keep coming out in slow motion with flat framing. What am I doing wrong?"
- "Make my character from ./cast/front.png and ./cast/side.png a Kling 4 element and write a 10-second take where he says "We're late""
